name: A Chiang Mai garden

place_source.title: Wikidata: Chiang Mai (Q52028), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A suburban garden plot on the western edge of Chiang Mai, northern Thailand: a lawn and border of palms, champaca and clipped hedges, where bulbuls and tailorbirds call from the shrubs, magpie-robins and mynas patrol the ground, Finlayson's squirrels run along the fence, and Asian common toads and house geckos come out after dark in the monsoon heat.

facts.text: Chiang Mai has a tropical savanna climate (Köppen Aw), warm to hot year-round with a pronounced dry season and a monsoon wet season.

source.title: Wikipedia: Chiang Mai
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Chiang Mai", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Chiang Mai is the largest city in northern Thailand and lies at an average elevation of about 300 m in the Thai highlands.

source.title: Wikipedia: Chiang Mai
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Chiang Mai", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city sits on the Ping River, a major tributary of the Chao Phraya, and the temple of Wat Phra That Doi Suthep stands on the mountain of the same name at 1,073 m to the north-west.

source.title: Wikipedia: Chiang Mai
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Chiang Mai", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The red-whiskered bulbul is a resident frugivore common in urban gardens and hill forests across tropical Asia, feeding on fruits and small insects and perching conspicuously on trees.

source.title: Wikipedia: Red-whiskered bulbul
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Red-whiskered bulbul", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The Asian common toad lives mostly in disturbed lowland habitats across South and Southeast Asia, breeds in still and slow-flowing water during the monsoon, and is often seen at night under street lamps.

source.title: Wikipedia: Duttaphrynus melanostictus
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Duttaphrynus melanostictus", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Finlayson's squirrel occurs in a wide range of wooded habitats in Thailand and neighbouring countries, including gardens and parks in cities, and is normally a canopy-dweller feeding mainly on fruit.

source.title: Wikipedia: Finlayson's squirrel
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Finlayson's squirrel", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
